title: Evaluation and quotient equations for origin adjunctions
statement: Let O be a commutative ring and ell in O. Fix compactification c of f:X->Y, etale support package S and exceptional adjunction G, actual site comparisons CX,CY,CZ, pro-etale support P and canonical compactification comparison R [def-pur-exceptional-system-transport-interfaces, def-coef-system-site-transport-interfaces, def-sf-strict-etale-exceptional-adjoint-interfaces]. Let record be transport data: its system and finite origin adjunctions satisfy the prescribed transpose formula and its evaluations preserve origins. Suppose each finite source-site counit is invertible on finite origin, and suppose evaluation of R equals the canonical finite comparison word. Then (1) evaluation of the system-origin adjunction unit followed by the right-evaluation comparison and the right image of the left-evaluation comparison is the finite-origin unit; (2) the left-evaluation comparison followed by the finite-left image of the right-evaluation comparison and then the finite-origin counit equals evaluation of the system-origin counit; (3) for each n<=m and arbitrary pro-etale system N, the scalar-derived image of the m right-etale-evaluation comparison, followed by inverse site tensor comparison, the site inverse of G's quotient comparison, and the site inverse of G_n applied to the input quotient transpose, equals the output quotient transpose followed by the n right-etale-evaluation comparison. The exact words and their order are displayed in lean.statement; all quotient transposes are on the unbounded categories.

source.place: Zheng Lemmas 4.10 and 5.22 and Proposition 5.24; Stacks 0B65.

proof.text: Evaluate the origin comparison, expanding its source-site counit. Naturality of exceptionalProSupportEvaluation, the assumed comparison evaluation square, CX.image.counit and naturality of exceptionalSystemLevelComparison identify its evaluation with the finite origin comparison, preceded by the inverse-site, support and direct-site evaluation comparisons.

The evaluated Hom transpose of an adjunction is obtained from its evaluated unit and naturality of the right evaluation comparison; for G use its prescribed evaluation-mate equation and adjunctionMate_transpose. Apply these identities to the three adjunctions in the origin Hom chain. The preceding comparison equation identifies the left-hand input words. Apply the system and finite ExceptionalOriginAdjunction.transpose fields, and cancel evaluation of the source-site counit, which is invertible by record.siteX.counit. This gives origin_hom_evaluation for every map, without inferring equality from evaluations.

For unit evaluation apply origin_hom_evaluation to the identity of the left image, and use homEquiv_id and right naturality of the finite Hom equivalence with the left-evaluation isomorphism. For counit evaluation apply it to the system counit. Its transpose is the identity; injectivity of the finite Hom equivalence, followed by homEquiv_counit and cancellation of the left-evaluation isomorphism, gives the displayed counit equation.

The recorded restrictedDirect_mate equation identifies the scalar/site conjugate of derivedTensor. The recorded restrictedInverse_mate equation and the iterated mate identity then identify restrictedInverse as the scalar-adjunction mate of inverse derivedTensor. Apply adjunctionMate_transpose to inverseTransition to obtain site_inverse_transition, an equation of actual unbounded scalar transposes.

Expand exceptionalSystemRightEtaleEvaluation. Move the evaluated etale-right comparison through inverse derivedTensor by naturality. Substitute G's given quotient transition equation, and then site_inverse_transition. Functoriality and associativity give exactly the displayed quotient equation on arbitrary systems. No tensor object is required to be bounded below.

proof_origin.place: Zheng Lemmas 4.10 and 5.22 and Proposition 5.24; formal adjunction calculation from the recorded interfaces, U7, 2026-10-28. The geometric existence and fixed-ring pullback-cube theorems are not reapplied.
